questions.question: How do you write SELECT queries in Rails (Active Record)?
questions.title: SQL Select Basics
questions.direct_answer: SELECT picks rows/columns from a table. In Active Record: `User.all` = `SELECT * FROM users`; `User.select(:id, :name)` = `SELECT id, name FROM users` (lean rows); `User.where(active: true)` adds WHERE; `User.order(created_at: :desc).limit(10)` adds ORDER/LIMIT. Chain them (returns an AR relation, lazy — runs the SQL when you force it: .to_a, .each, .count). `pluck(:email)` = `SELECT email FROM users` returning an array of values (not objects — fast for one column). `exists?(id: 1)` = `SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1` (boolean). `find(1)` (by id), `find_by(name: 'x')` (first match). For aggregates: `count`, `minimum(:age)`, `group(:role).count`. Use `select` to grab a few columns (less memory), `pluck` for just values (no objects), `where` to filter (parameterized/safe), and chain lazily. Avoid `User.all.to_a` (loads everything) on big tables — use `find_each(batch_size: 1000)` to stream in batches.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know the SELECT chain (where/order/limit/select/pluck), relations are lazy, and pluck/find_each for efficiency.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: User.all.to_a on a big table (loads everything) — use find_each to batch; or select * when you need a few columns (use select/pluck).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: SELECT chain: all/select, where (safe), order, limit, pluck (values), count. Lazy relations. Use find_each to batch big tables.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[relation: lazy] --> W[where: filter]
  W --> O[order/limit]
```

sections.title: SQL select basics
sections.content:
```ruby
# SELECT * FROM users
User.all                              # relation (lazy; SQL runs when forced)

# SELECT id, name FROM users  (lean rows -> less memory)
User.select(:id, :name)
User.select('id, name, age')

# WHERE (parameterized/safe):
User.where(active: true)              # WHERE active = TRUE
User.where('age > ?', 18)             # WHERE age > 18 (bound)
User.where(name: ['Al', 'Bo'])        # WHERE name IN ('Al','Bo')

# ORDER / LIMIT / OFFSET:
User.order(created_at: :desc).limit(10).offset(20)

# Chain (lazy relation): SQL runs when you force it
rel = User.where(active: true).order(:name)   # no SQL yet
rel.to_a          # -> SELECT ... (runs now)
rel.each { ... }  # -> runs
rel.count         # -> SELECT COUNT(*)

# Get values (not objects) -- fast for one column:
User.pluck(:email)          # ['a@x', 'b@y', ...]  (SELECT email)
User.pluck(:id, :name)      # [[1,'Al'], [2,'Bo'], ...]
User.distinct.pluck(:role)  # unique roles

# Lookups:
User.find(1)                # by primary key (raises if missing)
User.find_by(name: 'Al')    # first match (nil if none)
User.exists?(id: 1)         # SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1 (boolean)

# Aggregates:
User.count                  # SELECT COUNT(*)
User.minimum(:age)
User.group(:role).count     # { 'admin' => 2, 'user' => 50 }

# DON'T load a big table into memory:
#   User.all.to_a  # loads EVERYTHING
# Stream in batches instead:
User.find_each(batch_size: 1000) { |u| do_stuff(u) }   # SELECT ... LIMIT 1000 OFFSET ...

# Summary: select (columns), where (filter, safe), order/limit, pluck (values),
#          lazy chaining, find_each for big tables.
```

sections.title: What the interviewer wants
sections.content: Explain a repeatable debugging sequence: reproduce, isolate, observe, fix, and prove the fix. Tie each step to what How do you write SELECT queries in Rails (Active Record) is supposed to guarantee. SELECT picks rows/columns from a table. In Active Record: `User.all` = `SELECT * FROM users`; `User.select(:id, :name)` = `SELECT id, name FROM users` (lean rows); `User.where(active: true)` adds WHERE; `User.order(created_at: :desc).limit(10)` adds ORDER/LIMIT. Chain them (returns an AR relation, lazy — runs the SQL when you force it: .to_a, .each, .count). `pluck(:email)` = `SELECT email FROM users` returning an array of values (not objects — fast for one column). `exists?(id: 1)` = `SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1` (boolean). `find(1)` (by id), `find_by(name: 'x')` (first match). For aggregates: `count`, `minimum(:age)`, `group(:role).count`. Use `select` to grab a few columns (less memory), `pluck` for just values (no objects), `where` to filter (parameterized/safe), and chain lazily. Avoid `User.all.to_a` (loads everything) on big tables — use `find_each(batch_size: 1000)` to stream in batches.

SELECT picks rows/columns from a table.

In Active Record: `User.all` = `SELECT * FROM users`; `User.select(:id, :name)` = `SELECT id, name FROM users` (lean rows); `User.where(active: true)` adds WHERE; `User.order(created_at: :desc).limit(10)` adds ORDER/LIMIT.

Use `select` to grab a few columns (less memory), `pluck` for just values (no objects), `where` to filter (parameterized/safe), and chain lazily. sections.title: SQL select basics
sections.content:
```ruby
# SELECT * FROM users
User.all                              # relation (lazy; SQL runs when forced)

# SELECT id, name FROM users  (lean rows -> less memory)
User.select(:id, :name)
User.select('id, name, age')

# WHERE (parameterized/safe):
User.where(active: true)              # WHERE active = TRUE
User.where('age > ?', 18)             # WHERE age > 18 (bound)
User.where(name: ['Al', 'Bo'])        # WHERE name IN ('Al','Bo')

# ORDER / LIMIT / OFFSET:
User.order(created_at: :desc).limit(10).offset(20)

# Chain (lazy relation): SQL runs when you force it
rel = User.where(active: true).order(:name)   # no SQL yet
rel.to_a          # -> SELECT ... (runs now)
rel.each { ... }  # -> runs
rel.count         # -> SELECT COUNT(*)

# Get values (not objects) -- fast for one column:
User.pluck(:email)          # ['a@x', 'b@y', ...]  (SELECT email)
User.pluck(:id, :name)      # [[1,'Al'], [2,'Bo'], ...]
User.distinct.pluck(:role)  # unique roles

# Lookups:
User.find(1)                # by primary key (raises if missing)
User.find_by(name: 'Al')    # first match (nil if none)
User.exists?(id: 1)         # SELECT 1 ... LIMIT 1 (boolean)

# Aggregates:
User.count                  # SELECT COUNT(*)
User.minimum(:age)
User.group(:role).count     # { 'admin' => 2, 'user' => 50 }

# DON'T load a big table into memory:
#   User.all.to_a  # loads EVERYTHING
# Stream in batches instead:
User.find_each(batch_size: 1000) { |u| do_stuff(u) }   # SELECT ... LIMIT 1000 OFFSET ...

# Summary: select (columns), where (filter, safe), order/limit, pluck (values),
#          lazy chaining, find_each for big tables.
```
